links.comparator_used: ML models trained only on South American public spectra (published pipeline applied as-is) vs models retrained on pooled South American plus Kazakhstan spectra
links.outcome: Detection accuracy for Kazakhstan samples (SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, asymptomatic controls)
links.effect: SA-only random forest: 91.0% SARS-CoV-2+, 48.0% NCARI, 67.0% AC. Pooled SA-Kaz SVM-RBF: 88.0% SARS-CoV-2+, 95.0% NCARI, 78% AC; SARS-CoV-2 vs rest AUC 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; high accuracy maintained for South American samples.
links.tradeoff: Detection of SARS-CoV-2+ samples fell slightly (91.0% to 88.0%). Authors note continuous re-optimization will be needed as respiratory infections evolve. The two arms also used different top-performing algorithms (random forest vs SVM-RBF).
links.quote: Incorporation of spectral signatures from Kazakhstan substantially increased the accuracy of detection.

design_hint: local retraining with site-specific data before deployment
